prs.title: fix(client): avoid redundant fallback on root-like discovery paths
prs.author: raashish1601
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both rewrite the same trailing-slash-stripping code in buildWellKnownPath (and related discovery-path logic) that produces malformed/inconsistent well-known discovery paths. #2214 hardens buildWellKnownPath AND buildDiscoveryUrls to strip *all* trailing slashes via regex (fixing double-slash paths like '/foo//.well-known/...'), but leaves shouldAttemptFallback's `pathname === '/'` check untouched — that check is actually dead code today because the pathname it receives has already been stripped down to '' by the existing single-slash-strip logic, so the 'already at root' short-circuit never fires and every root-path discovery attempt performs a redundant fallback request. #2215 fixes exactly that: it extracts a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper (same trailing-slash regex as #2214) for buildWellKnownPath and corrects shouldAttemptFallback's comparison to `pathname === ''` to match what's actually produced, eliminating the redundant network call on root-path discovery. #2215 does not touch buildDiscoveryUrls's separate inline copy of the strip logic, so #2214's multi-slash hardening there is not duplicated by #2215. (2 PRs)

members.author: raashish1601
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2215: Both rewrite the same trailing-slash-stripping code in buildWellKnownPath (and related discovery-path logic) that produces malformed/inconsistent well-known discovery paths. #2214 hardens buildWellKnownPath AND buildDiscoveryUrls to strip *all* trailing slashes via regex (fixing double-slash paths like '/foo//.well-known/...'), but leaves shouldAttemptFallback's `pathname === '/'` check untouched — that check is actually dead code today because the pathname it receives has already been stripped down to '' by the existing single-slash-strip logic, so the 'already at root' short-circuit never fires and every root-path discovery attempt performs a redundant fallback request. #2215 fixes exactly that: it extracts a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper (same trailing-slash regex as #2214) for buildWellKnownPath and corrects shouldAttemptFallback's comparison to `pathname === ''` to match what's actually produced, eliminating the redundant network call on root-path discovery. #2215 does not touch buildDiscoveryUrls's separate inline copy of the strip logic, so #2214's multi-slash hardening there is not duplicated by #2215.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2215: Both rewrite the same trailing-slash-stripping code in buildWellKnownPath (and related discovery-path logic) that produces malformed/inconsistent well-known discovery paths. #2214 hardens buildWellKnownPath AND buildDiscoveryUrls to strip *all* trailing slashes via regex (fixing double-slash paths like '/foo//.well-known/...'), but leaves shouldAttemptFallback's `pathname === '/'` check untouched — that check is actually dead code today because the pathname it receives has already been stripped down to '' by the existing single-slash-strip logic, so the 'already at root' short-circuit never fires and every root-path discovery attempt performs a redundant fallback request. #2215 fixes exactly that: it extracts a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper (same trailing-slash regex as #2214) for buildWellKnownPath and corrects shouldAttemptFallback's comparison to `pathname === ''` to match what's actually produced, eliminating the redundant network call on root-path discovery. #2215 does not touch buildDiscoveryUrls's separate inline copy of the strip logic, so #2214's multi-slash hardening there is not duplicated by #2215.
